production.note: US model years 2024-2026. Start: 2024 model (The Drive's '2024 Chevy Corvette E-Ray' first drive; KBB, Sean Tucker, 17 Jan 2023: 'The E-Ray goes on sale in 2023', kbb-e-ray-news-2023). End year is provisional: Cars.com lists a 2026 Corvette E-Ray with '655 @ 6450' (carscom-e-ray-2026), and chevrolet.com's Corvette page (chevrolet-corvette-lineup-2027, at the /e-ray address) now lists Stingray, Grand Sport, Grand Sport X ('721 Combined horsepower'), Z06, ZR1 and ZR1X, with no E-Ray. No GM statement that the E-Ray ended with 2026 was found.

body.note: KBB: offered as a coupe (from $104,295) and a convertible (from $111,295). The coupe has a removable roof panel; the convertible is a retractable hardtop sold under the same E-Ray name.

configuration.note: '6.2-liter V8 with a front single-motor electric drive unit'

displacementL.note: '6.2-liter V8' (LT2). The cc figure was not on a page opened for this car.

aspiration.note: Naturally aspirated 6.2-liter LT2 V8 (no forced induction mentioned).

fuel.note: Full hybrid, not plug-in: '1.9-kWh lithium-ion battery' with a front electric motor. Car and Driver's panel gives the pack as "1.1-kWh liquid-cooled lithium-ion battery pack" (cd-corvette-e-ray-2024); The Drive's 1.9 kWh is not reconciled, and it does not affect the fuel type.

drivetrain.note: '8-speed dual-clutch automatic | all-wheel drive'; KBB: 'The electric motor powers the front wheels. The V8 powers the rear set.'

powerHp.note: Combined system output as printed in Car and Driver's road-test panel '2024 Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray*' (owner copy), quote: "pushrod V-8, aluminum block and heads, direct fuel injection, 495 hp, 470 lb-ft + 1 AC  motor, 160 hp, 125 lb-ft (combined output: 655 hp; 1.1-kWh liquid-cooled lithium-ion battery pack)". Publications agree: The Drive spec box (Peter Holderith, 13 Oct 2023): "655 (495 from V8 @ 6,450 rpm | 160 from electric motor)" (thedrive-e-ray-2023); KBB editorial (kbb-e-ray-news-2023, Sean Tucker): "a total of 655 horsepower"; Cars.com: 'SAE Net Horsepower @ RPM 655 @ 6450' (carscom-e-ray-2024). No Chevrolet page could be opened.

weightLb.note: Weight-order step 2: Car and Driver road-test curb weight (owner decision, 9 October 2026, docs/DATA_GUIDE.md); a measured weight of C/D's test car. Quote (C/D panel '2024 Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray*'): "Curb Weight: 3965 lb". Test car: "mid-engine, front-motor, front/all-wheel-drive, 2-passenger, 2 door targa" (the coupe with removable roof panel), "Transmission, F/R: direct-drive/8-speed dual-clutch automatic", "Base/As Tested: $106,595/$113,985", "Options: 2LE Equipment package, $5500; Carbon Flash forged aluminum wheels, $995; Performance package, $500; Black exhaust tips, $395" (printed '2LE'; the E-Ray trims on Cars.com are 1LZ to 3LZ). This curb weight replaces Chevrolet's DRY weight of 3,774 lb for the coupe (weight-order step 4), reported by The Drive ("Dry Weight | 3,774 pounds (coupe) | 3,856 pounds (convertible)") and Carscoops ("The E-Ray coupe's dry weight as 3,774 lbs (1,712 kg)"); see discrepancies. Never skip a step: a curb figure comes before a dry one.

discrepancies.reason: Dry vs curb: 3,774 lb is Chevrolet's dry weight for the coupe (Cars.com mislabels it curb); Car and Driver's 3,965 lb is the measured curb weight of an optioned test car.
discrepancies.resolution: Owner decision, 9 October 2026: the Car and Driver road-test curb weight is used (docs/DATA_GUIDE.md, Weight step 2). 3,965 lb curb used; the earlier record used the 3,774 lb dry figure (step 4) provisionally.

provisionalNote: Only the last model year is provisional: 2026 is inferred from Cars.com (a database listing a 2026 Corvette E-Ray) and chevrolet.com's current lineup, which no longer lists the E-Ray; a GM statement or release saying the E-Ray ended with the 2026 model year (or continues) would replace it. Power (655 hp combined) and weight (3,965 lb, Car and Driver road-test curb weight) now come from Car and Driver's road-test panel (owner decision, 9 October 2026) and are no longer provisional.
